title: Rav Ika bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav Chananel’s student, as in Kiddushin 72a: “Rav Ika bar Avin said that Rav Chananel said.” Abaye said to them: “Do not listen to him.” He said to him: “Is it mine? It is Rav Chananel’s, who said it in Rav’s name.” They went and asked Rav Chananel, who said to them, etc. Likewise in Megillah 3a: “Rav Ika bar Avin said that Rav Chananel said.” In Nedarim 77a he said that Rav attended to Rav Chananel (to release him from his vow); Hyman calls the Gemara’s reading erroneous: “to Rabbah,” but in Yuchasin it is correct. Seder HaDorot wondered how Abaye could ask Rav Chananel, and therefore says that he is Abaye Kashisha; Hyman objects that he overlooked that Abaye also saw Rav Yehudah, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: The vow procedure is release from the vow, not a husband’s annulment. Hyman’s Rav/Rabbah reading preference and chronology criticism remain attributed; no new Abaye identity is admitted.

The consulted Kiddushin 72a directly preserves Rav Ika bar Avin reporting Rav Chananel in Rav’s name and the exchange with Abaye. Release of a vow is distinct from a husband’s annulment. Hyman’s Nedarim Rav/Rabbah preference, Yuchasin reading and Abaye chronology criticism remain his; exact editions were not independently inspected here.
